note: v7 ignored plan mode. It returned no slots, so every request (about 460 ms apart) played one action for all 8 moments. All three games cleared the first cactus and died on the next one: the jump for it was judged 'early' at one request, and by the next request it was already too late. The jump key also stayed held for the whole jump, so a later press needed an extra plan just to release it. The new extractor measures time with nowMs, tracks the inputs in info.pending and the jump in progress, and returns 8 slot states, one predicted for each moment. jumpTiming now picks the best moment among the ones this plan and the next can still act on. It says 'early' when an input already scheduled clears the obstacle, and high birds are included in the jump check. After the plan's own press the next slots show the dino 'rising', then 'coasting' 150 ms later (past Chrome's jump cap, so letting go is harmless). One plan therefore presses and releases, and the next plan can jump again right after landing.
instructions:
Apply these rules in order and pick the first that matches.
1. If over is true: choose JUMP (restarts the game).
2. If player.phase is "rising": choose JUMP (keep the key held: letting go in the first 150 ms after take-off cuts the jump into a low hop that lands on the cactus).
3. If player.phase is "coasting": choose NOOP (let go of the key: from then on it no longer changes the jump, and the next jump needs a fresh press).
4. If threat is null: choose NOOP.
5. If threat.duckable is true and threat.near is true: choose DUCK (keep choosing it until the bird has passed).
6. If threat.jumpTiming is "ok" or "late": if jumpReady is false choose NOOP (let go of the held key first), otherwise choose JUMP.
7. Otherwise (jumpTiming "early" or "n/a"): choose NOOP and wait.
Notes: every field describes the game at the moment the action takes effect. In a plan, each moment has its own object in slots, predicted from the inputs already scheduled and from what these same rules choose at the plan's earlier moments. So after the moment that presses JUMP, the next moments show the dino rising and, 150 ms later, coasting: the plan lets go of the key there, and the next plan can press again right after landing. player.phase is ground / rising (the first 150 ms after take-off) / coasting (the rest of the jump). threat is the nearest obstacle that can still hit the dino (high birds, stars and the moon are left out; on the ground, obstacles already behind the dino are dropped). threat.dx is the gap in px from the dino's front to the obstacle, and threat.bottom is the obstacle's lowest point above the ground. threat.duckable is true for a bird at head height that the dino can duck under. threat.near is true when the obstacle reaches the dino within 250 ms, or is already alongside it. threat.jumpTiming comes from simulating a full jump (about 560 ms) pressed at this moment against the threat, the obstacle after it and any high bird. "early" means wait: a jump now would hit something, a later moment that can still act (the next moment of this plan, or the next plan) is safer, or an input already scheduled clears the threat. "ok" means jump now. "late" means no safe moment is left, so jump immediately anyway. "n/a" means not a jump case (a bird to duck under, or the dino is in the air). jumpReady is false while ducking and while the jump key is still held on the ground. speed is the ground speed in px per ms of game time.

actions.description: Press ArrowUp to jump from the ground (needs a fresh press); keep it held for the first 150 ms of the jump for full height; also restarts the game
Duck under mid-height birds (hold while the bird passes)

tests.why: Night-mode stars (9x9 sprites high in the sky) must never show up as obstacles.
A sky decoration must never become the threat that triggers a jump.
The star that caused the mistimed jump before the small cactus must be filtered out.
With only a star and an overhead bird ahead, the dino must stay on the ground instead of jumping into the bird.
When the dino lands before the large cactus, the threat must be the cactus rather than a star, so the jump is timed to the cactus.

v4 divided each decision's scroll by an assumed 30 ms while about 42 ms pass, so it reported 0.5-0.65 px/ms against a true value of about 0.44 and jumped too early. Speed is now ground scroll per game frame (frames counted from clouds, which drift 1 px per frame) divided by 16 ms.
The same speed fix, checked earlier in a game (about 4-7 s), where the ground moves 6-7 px per 16 ms frame.
Right after the fatal take-off (alt 31, then 40), the dino must be read as rising so that the jump key stays held.
The same check for the seed-303 death, where the jump was cut to a 54 px hop and came down on a small cactus.
All three v4 deaths were short hops caused by releasing ArrowUp about 40 ms after the press, just past Chrome's 30 px minimum jump height. The key must stay held while the dino is rising.

v5 died on seed 202 because the frames right after the duck press redraw only the dino, so the bird disappeared from the state, the duck was released and the dino stood up into the bird. Whenever the dino is ducking (or must release a key), the obstacle it reacts to must still be there, carried over from the last full frame.
v5 measured speed against cloud drift and reported 0.31-0.34 px/ms, while obstacles moved about 0.41 px/ms at 10-11 s (dx and gameMs agree). Speed is now ground scroll per ms of game time.

tests.expect: state.player === null || state.player.phase !== 'ground' || state.threat === null || state.threat.duckable === true || state.threat.dx > 30 || state.threat.jumpTiming !== 'early'
tests.why: With the underestimated speed, v5 kept jumpTiming 'early' until the cactus was at dx 15. It cleared that cactus but landed on the next one 250 px later. On the ground, a cactus within 30 px must never be 'early'.

tests.expect: state.player === null || state.player.phase !== 'ground' || state.threat === null || state.threat.duckable === true || state.threat.dx > 30 || state.threat.jumpTiming !== 'early'
tests.why: The same late-jump death on seed 303: 'early' at dx 24, a jump at dx 11, then a landing on the second small cactus. A cactus within 30 px must already be 'ok' or 'late'.

tests.expect: !state.slots || state.slots.every(function (s, i) { return i < 3 || [0, 1, 2, 3].some(function (d) { var q = state.slots[i - d]; return !q.player || q.player.phase !== 'rising'; }); })
tests.why: v7 held ArrowUp for the whole jump, so after landing a plan had to spend its one change on releasing the key, and the jump for the next cactus came a plan too late. The key must count as needed ('rising') for at most 150 ms after take-off (3 moments), so the plan that presses also releases it.

tests.expect: !state.slots || state.slots.every(function (s, i) { return i < 3 || [0, 1, 2, 3].some(function (d) { var q = state.slots[i - d]; return !q.player || q.player.phase !== 'rising'; }); })
tests.why: The same release check on seed 202, where the dino landed on the small cactus right behind the large one.
v7 returned no slots in plan mode, so one decision was played for all 8 moments. Every moment must get its own state with exactly the fields of the present state.

tests.expect: state.player === null || state.player.phase !== 'ground' || state.threat === null || state.threat.duckable === true || state.threat.jumpTiming !== 'n/a'
tests.why: On the ground, a threat that has to be jumped must always get a real timing (early/ok/late), including the obstacle that comes right after a landing.
